card.name: Which or whose after 'of'
card.fires_on: The relative word "which" (or "whose") right after "of" in a noun phrase such as "the fee for which" or "the lower layer of which". It is common in formal or descriptive prose.

modes.label: of which
modes.description: The relative pronoun "which" follows a noun and "of" or "for", and refers back to an earlier noun.
modes.example: the headwaters of<< which>> flow through the city of Springfield

modes.label: whose
modes.description: The relative "whose" follows "of" in a similar clause.
modes.example: the pursuit of<< whose>> profession necessitated frequent family removals

card.plain: It marks the point in a sentence where "of which" opens a clause that describes something just mentioned.
